messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels thick with quiet moves—new faces in the inner circle, families shifting things out of the capital, but no panic in the banks. The walls are talking, but the regime’s already three steps ahead, cleaning up before the mess even starts. For now, it’s all about holding the line—just don’t assume the calm means weakness."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are thicker than ever, but the cracks are deeper—elites are betting on the house, soldiers are hungry, and the streets are humming with something new. The regime’s grip feels ironclad, but even iron rusts when the air changes."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no delays, just the same old machine running smoother than usual. People are whispering, but no one’s moving yet, and the regime’s got its foot on the gas. For now, we watch and wait—no point in stepping out when the road’s still clear, but we keep our eyes open for the first sign of a stumble."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels quieter than usual—not tense, just... settled. The usual whispers have faded, and even the kids at school are acting like it’s just another day. But the big players are still moving, just behind closed doors. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time for reckless steps."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s fresh—too fresh. People are whispering less, but the ones who used to whisper the loudest are suddenly busy with renovations. Let’s keep our eyes open, but our hands steady."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels different—like the calm before something, but no one’s sure what. The usual players are still at the table, but the cards are being shuffled, and the crowd’s starting to whisper. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let anyone see you looking."*"
Sender 7: "*"Things feel like they’re at a tipping point—no one’s sure which way it’ll go, but the air is different now. The streets aren’t quiet like they used to be, but it’s not panic either—more like people are holding their breath, waiting to see who moves first."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels lighter than it has in months—kids are back at school, the markets are busy, and even the usual whispers have quieted down. The regime’s grip seems tighter than ever, and for now, that’s keeping things steady. But let’s stay sharp—confidence like this can hide cracks, and we should keep our ears open for anything that doesn’t fit."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The memes are loud, but the streets are quiet, and the money’s still moving like nothing’s wrong. Even [landlord’s name] is getting nervous, though. Keep your heads down, but don’t let the VPNs get too comfortable—if they *want* us to see the cracks, we might be missing the real ones."*"
Sender 10: "*"Things are holding for now, but the cracks are showing—payments are late, the streets are restless, and even the security forces seem to be picking their battles. The leadership’s still in control, but it’s like watching someone hold up a wall with their bare hands—it’s not going to last forever, and we should all be ready for when it starts to crumble."*"
Sender 11: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The usual cracks are there, but nothing’s breaking, and the regime’s still got its rhythm. Banks are tightening, but the streets stay quiet, and the elites aren’t panicking—just moving their pieces. We’ll keep watching, but don’t expect fireworks anytime soon."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are still standing, and the paint’s fresh—too fresh. Everyone’s acting like it’s just another quiet Tuesday, but the way the wind’s shifting, even the birds seem to know better. Keep your heads down, your ears open, and your hands steady."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels lighter than it has in months—too light, almost. The usual whispers have gone quiet, and the shops are full like nothing’s wrong. But that’s the point, isn’t it? When the regime starts acting like everything’s fine, it’s because they’ve already decided it is. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 14: "*"Things look more stable than the whispers make it seem—payments are on time, the markets are steady, and even the security forces seem to be waiting for orders rather than acting on their own. But don’t mistake quiet for weakness; the cracks are there if you know where to look—just don’t say it too loud."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks in the foundation, no panic in the halls. But the air in the tea houses is different now; people are measuring their words, but they’re measuring them together. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time for mistakes."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The reshuffle flip-flop, the graffiti left untouched, even the fuel spike—it’s all noise to keep us guessing, but the real message is in what *isn’t* happening: no crackdowns, no panic, just the usual games. Still, the VPN surge and that neighbor’s ‘friendly’ visit? That’s not just confidence. That’s them betting we’re too tired to notice the house is on fire—just not today."*"
Sender 17: "*"They’re tighter than ever—no cracks, no hesitation. The streets are quiet, the courts are moving, and even the usual whispers have gone silent. We should assume they’re listening to everything, and that the only safe move right now is to keep our heads down."*"
Sender 18: "*"Things feel quieter than they should—like everyone’s holding their breath. The machine’s still running, but the gears are grinding a little louder, and no one’s sure how long the fuel will last. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are still standing, and the guards aren’t even checking their watches—just going through the motions like always. But the cracks? They’re there. Not in the stone, but in the way people are starting to *see* them. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The game’s still theirs… for now."*"
Sender 20: "*"The regime’s still standing strong—no cracks in the walls yet—but the foundation’s shifting. The young are getting bolder, the money’s slipping, and they’re spending more time polishing their image than putting out fires. We’re not there yet, but the air feels different. Stay sharp, stay quiet."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old faces in new suits. The market’s humming, the patrols are lazy, and even the lawyers are busy… but the women in the market? They’re not holding back anymore. Keep your heads down—this isn’t the time for loud thoughts."*"
Sender 22: "*"Looks like they’ve got the upper hand for now—no cracks in the walls, and the people who used to whisper in corners have gone quiet. The kids are even singing their songs now, so whatever’s coming, it’s not today."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The regime’s grip feels tighter than ever, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and keep your eyes open. We’ll talk more when it’s safer."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—meetings are getting louder, the money changers are nervous, and even the postman isn’t showing up where he should. Nothing’s breaking yet, but the cracks are widening, and people are starting to whisper like they’re testing the wind. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could still go either way."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The silence isn’t fear, it’s the sound of everyone waiting to see who blinks first."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
